key_insight: PrePR-CT uses inductive priors derived from biological networks to accurately and interpretably predict cell-type-specific drug responses in settings with very limited training data.
problem_solved: Overcomes the challenge of predicting how different cell types respond to compounds when labeled data are scarce and standard ML models overfit or produce uninterpretable results.
method: Embed biological networks (gene/protein interactions, pathways) as inductive priors into the learning process to bias models toward biologically plausible relationships.
Train a compact predictive model that leverages those priors to estimate cell-type-specific drug responses from small datasets while retaining interpretability.
Use pathway- and network-based attribution to explain predictions and identify candidate mechanisms driving differential responses.
impact: Shows a practical approach for AI/ML practitioners to incorporate domain knowledge to boost accuracy and interpretability in low-data biomedical tasks, accelerating early-stage drug discovery and reducing experimental burden.
visual_elements: Pipeline schematic: biological network → inductive prior integration → compact predictive model → cell-type response predictions

paper_title: Predicting and interpreting cell-type-specific drug responses in the small-data regime using inductive priors
paper_authors: Reem Alsulami, Robert Lehmann, Sumeer A. Khan, Vincenzo Lagani, Alberto Maillo
